href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/5201229/lottie-woad">Lottie Woad</a> assured it. <a data-player-guid="1182b9e6-8cb3-7511-a48a-c82ab1c57620" href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/7424/carlota-ciganda">Carlota Ciganda</a> sealed it.</p><p>The Solheim Cup is back in the hands of Team Europe.</p><p>The blue wave came early in the Sunday singles at Bernardus Golf and never really went away, with Woad holing a putt from 2 feet on No. 17 to win her match and guarantee the Europeans would reach the 14½ points needed to reclaim the crystal trophy from the United States.</p><p>Woad punched the air and jumped into the arms of her teammates, who flooded onto the green in celebration.</p><p>Victory was official about 10 minutes later, when Ciganda, who had the decisive point when Europe retained the Solheim Cup in 2023, got her team past the winning target three years later. She completed a 4-and-2 victory over <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/10617/jennifer-kupcho">Jennifer Kupcho</a>, the feisty American who had roared "<em>Vamos!</em>" ("Let's go!") when <a href="/golf/story/_/id/49916041/jennifer-kupcho-sinks-unlikely-putts-even-solheim-cup">holing an outrageous 93-foot</a> putt on the way to beating Ciganda in the four-balls Saturday.</p><p>"Today I was really motivated to beat her," Ciganda said, "because I knew it was going to be important."</p><p>Strains of "Olé, Olé, Olé, Olé" drifted across the course as the last matches finished and the European team and staff celebrated with Champagne. Captain Anna Nordqvist, her assistants as well as the players and their caddies formed a line, put their arms over one another's shoulders, and walked as one up the 18th fairway toward the green where <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/9133/celine-boutier">Celine Boutier</a> -- the remaining European player on the course -- was wrapping up her match.</p><p>When Boutier finished, she piled into the mass celebrations.</p><p>The final score: Europe 15, the United States 13.</p><blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">THE MOMENT TEAM EUROPE RECLAIMED THE SOLHEIM CUP! 🇪🇺🏆<a href="https://x.com/hashtag/TeamEurope?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#TeamEurope</a> | <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/SolheimCup?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#SolheimCup</a> <a href="https://t.co/BrytRplVdc">pic.twitter.com/BrytRplVdc</a></p>— Solheim Cup Team Europe (@SolheimCupEuro) <a href="https://x.com/SolheimCupEuro/status/2099151776913985815?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">September 13, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script><p>To a backdrop of blue-and-yellow smoke, Nordqvist hoisted aloft the Solheim Cup on a podium in front of a first-tee grandstand filled with jubilant fans then gave each of her celebrating players and assistants a touch of the trophy.</p><p>"This feels so good," said Nordqvist, who announced her retirement from playing two weeks ago. "There's just been so much hard work this week and in the last two years leading up to this."</p><p>Europe has now won three of the past five editions, the only loss in that stretch coming in Virginia two years ago (along with a 14-14 tie in 2023). The U.S. team didn't have possession of the crystal trophy for long and is still without a win on the road since 2015.</p><p>"The Europeans played great today, and that's the way it goes," U.S. captain Angela Stanford said. "So their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did -- they came out and played well."</p><p>The teams were tied at 8-8 after two days and set out Sunday in heavy rain for the singles, with Europe going out fast, putting blue all over the scoreboard and ultimately winning six of the first eight matches.</p><p>Early wins for <a data-player-guid="95eacd4d-17d0-4492-47a5-2c1cdfb2e364" href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/7774/charley-hull">Charley Hull</a> and <a data-player-guid="bb92f003-6a8b-2809-a409-73c59f7bfc6d" href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/434661/linn-grant">Linn Grant</a> laid the platform for victory, the only wobble for Europe coming when U.S. player <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/8007/alison-lee">Alison Lee</a> came from 4 down after 11 holes to beat <a data-player-guid="81a9048d-ac84-f8d6-ccb4-97aa0a1af592" href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/442557/esther-henseleit">Esther Henseleit</a> 1 up for the greatest comeback in Solheim Cup history.</p><p>Rookies contributed massively for Europe all week and especially Sunday, with Woad, <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/5146642/nastasia-nadaud">Nastasia Nadaud</a> and <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/5396870/julia-lopez-ramirez">Julia Lopez Ramirez</a> all winning their singles matches.</p><div class="ad-300"><div class="ad-center"><div class="ad-slot ad-slot-incontent2 ad-wrapper" data-slot-type="incontent2" data-slot-kvps="pos=incontent2" data-independent="true"></div></div></div><p>"I think it's been one of the best teams that we've had in the last few years," Ciganda said. "Everyone [is] just a unit, a team. That's what Europe is about."</p><p>The U.S. leads the all-time series 11-8, with one draw.</p><p>A big part of the narrative of the week was the misfiring performances of Europe's highest-ranked players.</p><p>Hull and Woad, two English players, were paired in each of the first four sessions, a first for a Solheim Cup, and contributed a half-point.</p><p>Redemption came Sunday, with Hull leading from the front -- she beat <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/7891/megan-khang">Megan Khang</a>, previously undefeated in singles, 3 and 2 in Match 1 -- and Woad going 4 up after nine holes against <a href="https://www.espn.com/golf/player/_/id/4425587/auston-kim">Auston Kim</a> before winning 2 and 1.</p><p>"She's been playing so good this week and not really getting anything off of it," Nordqvist said of Woad. "But holing the winning putt, I don't think that's ever going to be hard to [forget] for her."</p>

21d Paolo Uggetti Tour Championship 2026: Top moments as Scottie Scheffler earns the victory 14d ESPN staff 'Motivated' Europe rocks U.S. in singles, takes Solheim Cup 3h Lowry one-putts way to 4-shot lead in Irish Open 22h Kupcho putts help U.S. even Solheim Cup entering final day 1d Europe builds 7-5 lead at Solheim Cup after Korda, Corpuz falter 1d Lowry's 62 sets course record, leads Irish Open 2d Europe, U.S. tied 4-4 at Solheim Cup after Ciganda's late heroics 2d Niemann leads, McIlroy 4 back as wind, slow play dominate Irish Open 3d Solheim Cup to begin with matchup between Korda, Hull 3d Top takeaways from LIV Golf's bankruptcy filings 3d Tisha Thompson McIlroy predicts LIV exodus after bankruptcy filing 3d ESPN U.S. Ryder Cup team changing qualifying criteria for 2027 matches 4d McIlroy: Trump visit adds attention to Irish Open, 'can only be a good thing' 4d LIV Golf officially files for bankruptcy protection; Rahm, Bryson owed millions 5d Mark Schlabach GB&I wins Walker Cup for first time since 2015 7d Lawrence rallies, wins European Masters playoff 7d Grehan delivers 1-point lead for GB&I over U.S. 8d Report: CEO, president exit Good Good after ad 11d Tiger's license suspended 5 years after plea deal 11d Mark Schlabach Court docs: Tiger plans to change plea in DUI case 12d Team Europe reclaims Solheim Cup with Sunday splash over U.S. Associated Press Multiple Authors Sep 13, 2026, 10:51 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions DEN BOSCH, Netherlands -- Lottie Woad assured it. Carlota Ciganda sealed it. The Solheim Cup is back in the hands of Team Europe. The blue wave came early in the Sunday singles at Bernardus Golf and never really went away, with Woad holing a putt from 2 feet on No. 17 to win her match and guarantee the Europeans would reach the 14½ points needed to reclaim the crystal trophy from the United States. Woad punched the air and jumped into the arms of her teammates, who flooded onto the green in celebration. Victory was official about 10 minutes later, when Ciganda, who had the decisive point when Europe retained the Solheim Cup in 2023, got her team past the winning target three years later. She completed a 4-and-2 victory over Jennifer Kupcho , the feisty American who had roared " Vamos! " ("Let's go!") when holing an outrageous 93-foot putt on the way to beating Ciganda in the four-balls Saturday. "Today I was really motivated to beat her," Ciganda said, "because I knew it was going to be important." Strains of "Olé, Olé, Olé, Olé" drifted across the course as the last matches finished and the European team and staff celebrated with Champagne. Captain Anna Nordqvist, her assistants as well as the players and their caddies formed a line, put their arms over one another's shoulders, and walked as one up the 18th fairway toward the green where Celine Boutier -- the remaining European player on the course -- was wrapping up her match. When Boutier finished, she piled into the mass celebrations. The final score: Europe 15, the United States 13. THE MOMENT TEAM EUROPE RECLAIMED THE SOLHEIM CUP! 🇪🇺🏆 #TeamEurope | #SolheimCup pic.twitter.com/BrytRplVdc — Solheim Cup Team Europe (@SolheimCupEuro) September 13, 2026 To a backdrop of blue-and-yellow smoke, Nordqvist hoisted aloft the Solheim Cup on a podium in front of a first-tee grandstand filled with jubilant fans then gave each of her celebrating players and assistants a touch of the trophy. "This feels so good," said Nordqvist, who announced her retirement from playing two weeks ago. "There's just been so much hard work this week and in the last two years leading up to this." Europe has now won three of the past five editions, the only loss in that stretch coming in Virginia two years ago (along with a 14-14 tie in 2023). The U.S. team didn't have possession of the crystal trophy for long and is still without a win on the road since 2015. "The Europeans played great today, and that's the way it goes," U.S. captain Angela Stanford said. "So their backs were against the wall, they had nothing to lose, and that's exactly what they did -- they came out and played well." The teams were tied at 8-8 after two days and set out Sunday in heavy rain for the singles, with Europe going out fast, putting blue all over the scoreboard and ultimately winning six of the first eight matches. Early wins for Charley Hull and Linn Grant laid the platform for victory, the only wobble for Europe coming when U.S. player Alison Lee came from 4 down after 11 holes to beat Esther Henseleit 1 up for the greatest comeback in Solheim Cup history. Rookies contributed massively for Europe all week and especially Sunday, with Woad, Nastasia Nadaud and Julia Lopez Ramirez all winning their singles matches. "I think it's been one of the best teams that we've had in the last few years," Ciganda said. "Everyone [is] just a unit, a team. That's what Europe is about." The U.S. leads the all-time series 11-8, with one draw. A big part of the narrative of the week was the misfiring performances of Europe's highest-ranked players. Hull and Woad, two English players, were paired in each of the first four sessions, a first for a Solheim Cup, and contributed a half-point. Redemption came Sunday, with Hull leading from the front -- she beat Megan Khang , previously undefeated in singles, 3 and 2 in Match 1 -- and Woad going 4 up after nine holes against Auston Kim before winning 2 and 1. "She's been playing so good this week and not really getting anything off of it," Nordqvist said of Woad. "But holing the winning putt, I don't think that's ever going to be hard to [forget] for her." the surprise campaigns that prove vital to a team's playoff hopes. It can be young players showing dramatic improvement. It can be veterans who unexpectedly figure things out or just have a year where everything clicks.</p><p>Last week we looked at the <a href="/mlb/story/_/id/49815111/mlb-2026-fallen-stars-bad-gameplay-injuries-impact-raleigh-judge-skenes-vlad-jr">fallen stars of 2026</a> and the impact their down seasons had on their teams. Now, let's look at 10 players who leveled up this year how their seasons have changed the fortunes of their teams.</p><p><em>(For each player, we'll include their preseason projections from FanGraphs and then their current stats with Baseball-Reference WAR.)</em></p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/mil.png&h=60&w=60" SO, 1.8 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> 14-5, 1.95 ERA, 161.1 IP, 236 SO, 5.5 WAR</p><aside class="inline editorial float-r" data-behavior="article_related"><h2 Our MLB experts make final-month predictions</a><div class="editorial--metadata"><span class="author">ESPN</span></div></h2></li></ul><div class="button button-alt sm btn-related">2 Related</div></aside><p>It's easy to say that we all saw this coming, but absolutely nobody saw <em>this</em> coming -- the absolute dominance, the 1,000-plus pitches at 100 mph or faster, including one at 105.5 mph, the fastest ever by a starting pitcher in the Statcast era. The preseason projections viewed Misiorowski as a talented but erratic young starter, which is what he was in 2025. Instead, in 2026, he has learned to keep his delivery in sync and improved his ability to command that blistering four-seamer.</p><p>Consider this: Misiorowski has walked 6.7% of the batters he faced; it took the incomparable control artist Greg Maddux until his fifth season before he got his walk rate below that. With that combination of stuff and control, Misiorowski has held batters to a .156 average, which would be the lowest ever by a starting pitcher.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Brewers' fortunes:</strong> Milwaukee's top four starters last season were <a data-player-guid="aa1cac72-2915-387f-9e32-4b2f84f52b1d" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/39825/freddy-peralta">Freddy Peralta</a>, who was traded in the offseason to the <a href="/mlb/team/_/name/nym/new-york-mets">New York Mets</a>; <a data-player-guid="320d3bc5-be84-3c59-b976-399ebbb453a6" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/42449/quinn-priester">Quinn Priester</a>, who has sat out  the season because of injuries; <a data-player-guid="d4e26cc9-cade-3065-9574-dbc3139e247c" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/5131708/chad-patrick">Chad Patrick</a>, who has pitched primarily in relief; and <a data-player-guid="799067c0-7173-3a04-9e55-89171a4613b0" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/32106/jose-quintana">Jose Quintana</a>, who signed with the <a data-clubhouse-guid="f3f1ba71-05f1-a49a-0363-3b1d8e0db4cf" href="/mlb/team/_/name/col/colorado-rockies">Colorado Rockies</a> as a free agent. Those four starters combined for 104 starts for the Brewers in 2025 but only six in 2026 -- and yet, with an almost complete turnover in the rotation, Milwaukee starters rank fifth in the majors in ERA.</p><p>Misiorowski has led the way, of course, not only giving them an ace but also a better-than-forecasted workload, as he should end up with 180 innings or so. Without him leveling up, Chicago would be a lot closer to first place in the NL Central.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/chc.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="dcbeba5a-3fe9-3bf0-9f19-c077ef2a6f78" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4717833/pete-crow-armstrong">Pete Crow-Armstrong</a>, CF, <a data-clubhouse-guid="5cda5067-7075-66b1-4b94-2333ab8d9807" href="/mlb/team/_/name/chc/chicago-cubs">Chicago Cubs</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> .252/.303/.456, 26 HR, 4.7 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> .281/.375/.574, 41 HR, 9.2 WAR</p><p>It's hard to improve on a 5.9-WAR season, which is what PCA put together last year when he finished ninth in the MVP voting, but he has soared past that with one of the best seasons in Cubs history in 2026. Nobody doubted his Gold Glove defense, but skeptics -- and projections -- saw a poor strikeout-to-walk ratio (155-to-29) and second-half slide (.634 OPS) and wondered about his offensive upside.</p><p>Crow-Armstrong got off to a slow start, with a .659 OPS through May 20, including 54 strikeouts and 15 walks. Then everything clicked. He made some mechanical changes, lowering his hands, standing more upright and instituting a bigger stride. No doubt, those changes have helped <a href="/mlb/story/_/id/49779979/pete-crow-armstrong-adds-2-more-hrs-cubs-fall-reds">steer his production to MVP level</a>, but he also started being more selective on his swings:</p><p>2025: 60.1% swing rate, 41.6% chase rate, 5.34 SO/BB ratio<br />
2026 through May 20: 53.8% swing rate, 40.6% chase rate, 3.6 SO/BB ratio<br />
2026 after May 20: 47.5% swing rate, 31% chase rate, 1.95 SO/BB ratio</p><aside class="inline float-r inline-track"><h2 class="img-title">Awards Watch</h2><img data-lazyload="true" data-src="https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0823/r1705940_608x342_16-9.jpg" class="round lazyload"><p>What can Ohtani do to pass PCA for NL MVP? Cease or Schlittler for AL Cy Young? Here's the latest on MLB's awards races. <a href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/49672771/mlb-2026-awards-watch-august-mvp-cy-young-al-nl-rookie-manager-year-ohtani-pca">Bradford Doolittle &#187</a></p>
</aside><p>Those improved swing decisions, in combination with his best-in-the-business defense, suggest PCA's breakout is the real deal -- and that he should <a href="/mlb/story/_/id/49672771/mlb-2026-awards-watch-august-mvp-cy-young-al-nl-rookie-manager-year-ohtani-pca">be an MVP contender</a> for years to come.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Cubs' fortunes:</strong> With PCA leading the way, the Cubs lead the majors in runs scored, as the offense has carried a pitching staff that has faced a long list of injuries in both the rotation and bullpen. Even though several Cubs regulars haven't hit as well as last season -- <a data-player-guid="52d0b18a-1810-3aa6-b963-84ecef72a66d" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/42415/michael-busch">Michael Busch</a>, <a data-player-guid="b21d3016-6ad6-93a3-cb4a-24b46fa4f601" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/41219/nico-hoerner">Nico Hoerner</a>, <a data-player-guid="a004a121-0eb2-f885-7517-73688de8e933" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/34895/dansby-swanson">Dansby Swanson</a> -- they're still on pace to score about 60 more runs than in 2025. That hasn't been enough to keep pace with the Brewers, but it has kept Chicago comfortably in a wild-card position.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/nyy.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="58c38e07-3888-3b56-b9f6-6c6f4b1e9a20" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/5134581/cam-schlittler">Cam Schlittler</a>, RHP, <a data-clubhouse-guid="2b9cedf3-ce60-0bcf-fafe-8cd055255685" href="/mlb/team/_/name/nyy/new-york-yankees">New York Yankees</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> 8-7, 4.01 ERA, 120 IP, 119 SO, 1.7 WAR</p><p><strong>Season to date:</strong> 13-6, 2.01 ERA, 178.2 IP, 220 SO, 6.6 WAR</p><p>Schlittler's rise the past two years from unheralded prospect to Cy Young favorite has been phenomenal. He's putting together one of the best seasons ever for a Yankees starter -- no small achievement, given the franchise has had more than a little success in its history. He has given up one run or no runs in 20 of his 30 starts, already a franchise record, and has done so riding a heavy arsenal of upper 90s fastballs. He has thrown his four-seamer, cutter or sinker a combined 89.4% of his pitches -- and the league hasn't figured him out yet, as he has given up more than one run only once in his past nine starts.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Yankees' fortunes:</strong> <a data-player-guid="e3e39e69-2861-f5b5-49be-b0880534c802" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/33192/aaron-judge">Aaron Judge</a>? Injured for much of the season. <a data-player-guid="00ce805c-4c3d-c1c9-ab93-a6410f947e7b" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/32685/max-fried">Max Fried</a>? Sat out nearly half the season. <a data-player-guid="a1c10777-a90b-1d32-94ba-5e5ac51f4eab" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/33696/carlos-rodon">Carlos Rodon</a>? Sat out more than half the season. <a data-player-guid="af61347b-c222-7604-92c0-be4da7756430" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/32081/gerrit-cole">Gerrit Cole</a>? Didn't make his first start until May 22. With that group of stars missing a lot of time, Schlittler probably deserves MVP consideration aside from the Cy Young Award. He has been the dominant force all season in a rotation that leads the majors in ERA. As the offense struggled without Judge, Schlittler helped keep the Yankees within shouting distance of the <a data-clubhouse-guid="f8a579c6-08b9-7584-141d-317d0645763b" href="/mlb/team/_/name/tb/tampa-bay-rays">Tampa Bay Rays</a> in the American League East.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/cle.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="b27aebe1-3a75-30dd-8cbf-6222103d32ee" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4619898/parker-messick">Parker Messick</a>, LHP, <a data-clubhouse-guid="6ad8fa03-36bc-baab-c76a-345b6544424d" href="/mlb/team/_/name/cle/cleveland-guardians">Cleveland Guardians</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> 7-8, 4.04 ERA, 129 IP, 118 SO, 1.4 WAR</p><p><strong>Season to date:</strong> 11-9, 2.53 ERA, 167 IP, 173 SO, 5.4 WAR</p><p>Messick looked good in seven late-season starts in 2025, maintaining his rookie status for 2026, but with a fastball that had averaged 92.8 mph, he was viewed as more of a crafty lefty who might provide rotation depth rather than a potential frontline starter. Instead, he has been one of the league's top starters this season. And that fastball? He has pumped his four-seamer velocity up to 94.3 mph. Via Statcast pitch value metrics, it has been the most valuable pitch in baseball at plus-26 runs saved -- one run better even than Misiorowski's four-seam fastball.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Guardians' fortunes</strong>: The rotation has kept the Guardians in the hunt for the AL Central title and a wild-card spot, ranking eighth in ERA and fourth in innings, as the offense and bullpen have had issues. Not only has Messick been excellent, he also has been durable, with the most innings by a rookie pitcher since 2019. As the Guardians have inched closer to the White Sox, Messick has been at his best, with a 2.05 ERA since the beginning of July.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/cws.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="e98732ca-f76f-3831-8f7f-fdb3a8603001" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/42453/miguel-vargas">Miguel Vargas</a>, 3B, <a data-clubhouse-guid="8f4800c6-3c05-b3d5-8186-9750cd72a3c2" href="/mlb/team/_/name/chw/chicago-white-sox">Chicago White Sox</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> .238/.329/.406, 18 HR, 2.2 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> .248/.359/.477, 30 HR, 4.3 WAR</p><aside class="inline float-r inline-track"><h2 class="img-title">MLB playoff tracker 2026</h2><img data-lazyload="true" data-src="https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0821/mbl_probs_608x342.jpg" class="round lazyload"><p>From current playoff matchups and clinching scenarios to league races and the postseason schedule, we've got it all. <a href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/49752366/mlb-2026-playoff-tracker-clinch-scenarios-postseason-bracket-schedule">All things October &#187</a></p>
</aside><p>Vargas was coming off a 1.9-WAR season with the White Sox in 2025, and the forecasts predicted more of the same. Vargas has instead powered his way to a 30-homer season thanks primarily to one simple change: He's swinging harder. His average bat speed has jumped from 70.6 mph to 74 mph, which has resulted in harder contact and more balls flying over the fence. The key is that he has maintained his reasonably low strikeout rate while also improving his walk rate. He also leads the AL in runs scored, which no White Sox player has done in a full season since Johnny Mostil in 1925 (<a data-player-guid="295d1d4b-060d-d504-4651-287e9bf4b50e" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/33184/tim-anderson">Tim Anderson</a> tied for the lead in the 60-game season in 2020 and Frank Thomas led in the strike-shortened 1994 season).</p><p><strong>How he has changed the White Sox's fortunes:</strong> The White Sox ranked 23rd in the majors with 165 home runs in 2025 -- and 27th in runs scored. With Vargas, <a data-player-guid="6db99332-c2e8-3eec-aa42-171f22456ee6" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4872685/colson-montgomery">Colson Montgomery</a> and <a data-player-guid="37da30e0-9b6a-31a8-b783-083261547d7a" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4872595/munetaka-murakami">Munetaka Murakami</a> all having reached 30 home runs, the White Sox have hit 190 so far this season, which ranks sixth in the majors, and rank seventh in runs scored. The improved offense has ignited one of the most surprising seasons in White Sox history, with the club on the verge of making the playoffs only two years after a record-setting losing season in 2024.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/stl.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="f1c65de6-25d4-3aae-a3ba-f612a18d2829" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4684778/jordan-walker">Jordan Walker</a>, RF, <a data-clubhouse-guid="c781e7c6-2c5b-beaf-55b8-999c76f76661" href="/mlb/team/_/name/stl/st-louis-cardinals">St. Louis Cardinals</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> .239/.303/.387, 15 HR, 0.5 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> .282/.338/.490, 28 HR, 3.7 WAR</p><p>Once a top-10 overall prospect in the game, Walker hit well as a 21-year-old rookie in 2023 but then struggled the next two seasons with a .211 average and 69 OPS+. Expectations weren't high for 2026 -- even though he just turned 24 in May -- but he finally translated his elite bat speed into some big numbers, including reaching 100 RBIs, pulling the ball in the air more often and making a big improvement against off-speed pitches and breaking balls.</p><p>There is still room for improvement here as his chase rate (16th percentile) and whiff rate (12th percentile) lead to strikeouts and too many ground balls. His poor range in right field also drags down his overall WAR, although he does possess a powerful arm. If he can show PCA-like improvement in his swing decisions, Walker will do even more damage in the future.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Cardinals' fortunes:</strong> The Cardinals have exceeded expectations and hung close all season in the wild-card race, although it will take a miracle run to finish the regular season to grab a spot. Still, with Walker, <a data-player-guid="42a58ee8-69e4-392a-b71a-a798ebb7fd26" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4941056/jj-wetherholt">JJ Wetherholt</a> and <a data-player-guid="c587daab-66e6-39cb-a3cf-6f8f02f8fdd5" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4345070/alec-burleson">Alec Burleson</a>, there is now a young offensive foundation -- and Wetherholt and <a data-player-guid="e8ab6f85-80c5-3a0d-8ca8-f2ae943f5eb8" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4683365/masyn-winn">Masyn Winn</a> might both win Gold Gloves for their sterling up-the-middle defense. The Cardinals have been searching for a young power hitter to build around since Albert Pujols, and Walker looks as if he'll be that guy.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/sd.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="53b65b61-99f4-b102-24c1-7138251ddd24" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/35591/ty-france">Ty France</a>, 1B, <a data-clubhouse-guid="4dec648c-3eb9-055c-aebc-2711f30975a0" href="/mlb/team/_/name/sd/san-diego-padres">San Diego Padres</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> .251/.320/.380, 3 HR, 0.2 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> .290/.360/.507, 20 HR, 4.2 WAR</p><p>Our first veteran on the list, France has had good seasons in the past, including a 4.2-WAR season with the <a data-clubhouse-guid="56d60582-088f-6848-5180-1fb04440cf87" href="/mlb/team/_/name/sea/seattle-mariners">Seattle Mariners</a> in 2021, but he was worth just 0.4 WAR over the past two years as he played for four different teams. The Padres didn't even sign France until the middle of February -- and then only on a minor league contract. He made the roster after a strong spring training but started only one of the Padres' first 15 games before eventually becoming the starting first baseman.</p><aside class="inline float-r inline-track"><h2 class="img-title">Ranking MLB playoff races</h2><img data-lazyload="true" data-src="https://a.espncdn.com/photo/2026/0831/r1709561_608x342_16-9.jpg" class="round lazyload"><p>Here's what you need to know about the battles to reach October as teams try to lock up a postseason spot. <a href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/story/_/id/49784298/mlb-2026-playoffs-rankings-races-september-division-wild-card-top-seeds-byes">David Schoenfield &#187</a></p>
</aside><p>What kind of season has he had? He's second to only <a data-player-guid="e739e323-7ff4-bc6c-de71-f48ffcfaa329" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/32532/willson-contreras">Willson Contreras</a> in WAR among all major league first basemen. The key: France has focused on hitting for more power, not only pulling the ball more often but hitting it harder when he does hit it in the air. He has done that while seeing his always-solid strikeout rate rise only five percentage points.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Padres' fortunes:</strong> "I don't think anybody would have guessed that coming out of spring training," manager Craig Stammen said earlier this season about France's success. Indeed, he has been the Padres' best hitter -- and while the lineup has been excellent since the All-Star break, it flailed before that, so France especially helped keep the Padres afloat in the first half.</p><p>They had ranked in the middle of the pack in offense at first base in 2025, but that was mostly <a data-player-guid="b87dd56f-f15e-897b-b6a6-1ce6491b150a" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/39572/luis-arraez">Luis Arraez</a>, who left as a free agent. France has filled what could have turned into a black hole, and without him, the Padres would be several wins behind the Diamondbacks in the wild-card race instead of neck-and-neck for that final spot.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/ari.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="cb4a343b-ff08-86bb-5449-9fb473c21bad" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/32675/eduardo-rodriguez">Eduardo Rodriguez</a>, LHP, <a data-clubhouse-guid="43e14a76-ff66-49ed-24fc-2835932f99dd" href="/mlb/team/_/name/ari/arizona-diamondbacks">Arizona Diamondbacks</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> 8-8, 4.21 ERA, 133 IP, 119 SO, 1.3 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> 15-5, 2.55 ERA, 173 IP, 128 SO, 5.3 WAR</p><p>Coming off their World Series appearance in 2023, the Diamondbacks signed the eight-year veteran Rodriguez to a four-year, $80 million contract. The first two years didn't go well, as he went a combined 12-13, making only 10 starts in 2024, and had an ERA over 5.00 in each. This season has probably been a little fluky as he has given up a .269 average on balls in play -- well below his career mark of .304 -- and posted a 2.55 ERA despite a low strikeout rate. But he has made some changes to his pitch usage, throwing his changeup and curveball more often while dropping his four-seamer and cutter usage. That seems to have helped the effectiveness of his four-seamer, as batters are hitting .200 against it after a .287 average in 2025.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Diamondbacks' fortunes:</strong> They would be planning their offseason golf dates without him. The rest of the starting pitchers have combined for only 1.4 WAR and have gone 31-40. Lucky or not, Rodriguez's ERA is real -- and the Diamondbacks have gone 13-3 in his past 16 starts.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/mil.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="fb61ce47-001c-a99c-eab5-77eb5c782968" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/35013/jake-bauers">Jake Bauers</a>, 1B/OF, Milwaukee Brewers</strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> .220/.322/.420, 12 HR, 0.7 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> .268/.395/.490, 24 HR, 3.0 WAR</p><p>Bauers was an interesting prospect, reaching Triple-A at age 21 in the Rays' system, but he had never posted an above-average OPS+ in the majors until last season. Indeed, it's surprising the Brewers kept him around after he hit .199 in 2024. Now 30 years old, you can't really classify this as a breakout, but his Statcast page has red all over it: 96th percentile hard-hit rate, 94th percentile bat speed, 98th percentile walk rate, 96th percentile in expected wOBA. He leads the National League in OBP and ranks seventh in the majors in OPS. Maybe it's a career season, but there is nothing lucky about how he's putting up the numbers.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Brewers' fortunes:</strong> The Brewers are still last in the majors in home runs, but Bauers leads the team while ranking second to <a data-player-guid="0240a799-e19c-f126-76e2-8ff3bdc72c25" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/41179/brice-turang">Brice Turang</a> in RBIs despite playing mostly against just right-handers. Like several of his teammates, he has performed exceptionally well with runners in scoring position, with a .989 OPS. He's also hitting .326 with a .991 OPS in high-leverage plate appearances, helping the Brewers to rank third in runs despite that lack of over-the-fence pop.</p><p>Though he's not a good defensive player, Bauers has at least provided versatility, starting 75 games at first base and 39 in the outfield. He's not the team MVP with Misiorowski around, but Bauers has given the Brewers a legitimate middle-of-the-order hitter against right-handed pitching.</p><hr><img alt="" class="floatleft" src="https://a.espncdn.com/combiner/i?img=/i/teamlogos/mlb/500/tor.png&h=60&w=60" width="30"><h2><strong><a data-player-guid="bfefe680-2ff8-3cff-b94c-78998580944c" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/4917888/louis-varland">Louis Varland</a>, RHP, <a data-clubhouse-guid="0151aed9-9f11-ceae-195d-180ca603b64a" href="/mlb/team/_/name/tor/toronto-blue-jays">Toronto Blue Jays</a></strong></h2><p><strong>Preseason:</strong> 4-3, 2 saves, 3.51 ERA, 0.6 WAR</p><p><strong>2026 to date:</strong> 5-5, 33 saves, 1.26 ERA, 3.4 WAR</p><aside class="inline float-r inline-track"><h2 class="img-title">Postseason Baseball Challenge</h2><p><a href="https://fantasy.espn.com/games/mlb-postseason-challenge-2026/make-picks?addata=postseasonbaseballchallenge2026_mlb_web_inline" target="_blank"><img alt="" class="imageLoaded" src="https://chui-assets-cdn.espn.com/e543e3eb-517f-45ac-a7fc-4ac2463b43e6.jpeg" width="100%"></a></p><p>Fill out MLB postseason brackets for FREE! $10K in prizes. <b><a href="https://fantasy.espn.com/games/mlb-postseason-challenge-2026/make-picks?addata=postseasonbaseballchallenge2026_mlb_web_inline" target="_blank">Make Your Picks</a></b></p>
</aside><div class="ad-300"><div class="ad-center"><div class="ad-slot ad-slot-incontent2 ad-wrapper" data-slot-type="incontent2" data-slot-kvps="pos=incontent2" data-independent="true"></div></div></div><p>Considering how the Blue Jays' 2025 season ended -- with <a data-player-guid="9ee76eaf-6161-cfe8-0c5a-6544c83ad2d1" href="https://www.espn.com/mlb/player/_/id/33841/jeff-hoffman">Jeff Hoffman</a> unable to close out the lead in Game 7 of the World Series -- the ninth inning was going to be a key issue for the Jays this year. Hoffman started the season in the closer role again, but after three blown saves by mid-April, Varland took over and has produced one of the best relief seasons in Blue Jays' history, pumping 99-mph fastballs, a knuckle-curveball and a near-unhittable changeup. That combo has induced a high rate of grounders -- 97th percentile -- that has kept the ball in the park (only two home runs given up), a nice change from Hoffman's home run issues last season.</p><p><strong>How he has changed the Blue Jays' fortunes</strong>: If Varland hadn't stepped up, who knows where the Jays would be. Yes, the mediocrity across the AL has kept them in the wild-card race, but considering the lineup has struggled all season and the rotation has battled injuries, the bullpen has been one area that manager John Schneider has been able to trust after those initial issues in April.</p>

Arizona Diamondbacks 4h ESPN Fantasy baseball news: Jac may be back for Royals, Twins promote top prospect 7h ESPN Fantasy 10 MLB players who leveled up in 2026 -- and their team impact From Cam Schlittler to Miz and PCA, these players took their game to new heights in 2026 -- and their clubs found success because of it.  Elsa/Getty Images David Schoenfield Sep 11, 2026, 07:00 AM ET Close Covers MLB for ESPN.com Former deputy editor of Page 2 Been with ESPN.com since 1995 Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions One of the compelling features of any baseball season is the surprise campaigns that prove vital to a team's playoff hopes. It can be young players showing dramatic improvement. It can be veterans who unexpectedly figure things out or just have a year where everything clicks. Last week we looked at the fallen stars of 2026 and the impact their down seasons had on their teams. Now, let's look at 10 players who leveled up this year how their seasons have changed the fortunes of their teams. (For each player, we'll include their preseason projections from FanGraphs and then their current stats with Baseball-Reference WAR.) Jacob Misiorowski , RHP, Milwaukee Brewers Preseason: 9-8, 3.99 ERA, 135 IP, 155 SO, 1.8 WAR 2026 to date: 14-5, 1.95 ERA, 161.1 IP, 236 SO, 5.5 WAR Editor's Picks 2026 MLB core rankings: Who has the most star talent? Our MLB experts make final-month predictions ESPN 2 Related It's easy to say that we all saw this coming, but absolutely nobody saw this coming -- the absolute dominance, the 1,000-plus pitches at 100 mph or faster, including one at 105.5 mph, the fastest ever by a starting pitcher in the Statcast era. The preseason projections viewed Misiorowski as a talented but erratic young starter, which is what he was in 2025. Instead, in 2026, he has learned to keep his delivery in sync and improved his ability to command that blistering four-seamer. Consider this: Misiorowski has walked 6.7% of the batters he faced; it took the incomparable control artist Greg Maddux until his fifth season before he got his walk rate below that. With that combination of stuff and control, Misiorowski has held batters to a .156 average, which would be the lowest ever by a starting pitcher. How he has changed the Brewers' fortunes: Milwaukee's top four starters last season were Freddy Peralta , who was traded in the offseason to the New York Mets ; Quinn Priester , who has sat out the season because of injuries; Chad Patrick , who has pitched primarily in relief; and Jose Quintana , who signed with the Colorado Rockies as a free agent. Those four starters combined for 104 starts for the Brewers in 2025 but only six in 2026 -- and yet, with an almost complete turnover in the rotation, Milwaukee starters rank fifth in the majors in ERA. Misiorowski has led the way, of course, not only giving them an ace but also a better-than-forecasted workload, as he should end up with 180 innings or so. Without him leveling up, Chicago would be a lot closer to first place in the NL Central. Pete Crow-Armstrong , CF, Chicago Cubs Preseason: .252/.303/.456, 26 HR, 4.7 WAR 2026 to date: .281/.375/.574, 41 HR, 9.2 WAR It's hard to improve on a 5.9-WAR season, which is what PCA put together last year when he finished ninth in the MVP voting, but he has soared past that with one of the best seasons in Cubs history in 2026. Nobody doubted his Gold Glove defense, but skeptics -- and projections -- saw a poor strikeout-to-walk ratio (155-to-29) and second-half slide (.634 OPS) and wondered about his offensive upside. Crow-Armstrong got off to a slow start, with a .659 OPS through May 20, including 54 strikeouts and 15 walks. Then everything clicked. He made some mechanical changes, lowering his hands, standing more upright and instituting a bigger stride. No doubt, those changes have helped steer his production to MVP level , but he also started being more selective on his swings: 2025: 60.1% swing rate, 41.6% chase rate, 5.34 SO/BB ratio 2026 through May 20: 53.8% swing rate, 40.6% chase rate, 3.6 SO/BB ratio 2026 after May 20: 47.5% swing rate, 31% chase rate, 1.95 SO/BB ratio Awards Watch What can Ohtani do to pass PCA for NL MVP? Cease or Schlittler for AL Cy Young? Here's the latest on MLB's awards races. Bradford Doolittle &#187 Those improved swing decisions, in combination with his best-in-the-business defense, suggest PCA's breakout is the real deal -- and that he should be an MVP contender for years to come. How he has changed the Cubs' fortunes: With PCA leading the way, the Cubs lead the majors in runs scored, as the offense has carried a pitching staff that has faced a long list of injuries in both the rotation and bullpen. Even though several Cubs regulars haven't hit as well as last season -- Michael Busch , Nico Hoerner , Dansby Swanson -- they're still on pace to score about 60 more runs than in 2025. That hasn't been enough to keep pace with the Brewers, but it has kept Chicago comfortably in a wild-card position. Cam Schlittler , RHP, New York Yankees Preseason: 8-7, 4.01 ERA, 120 IP, 119 SO, 1.7 WAR Season to date: 13-6, 2.01 ERA, 178.2 IP, 220 SO, 6.6 WAR Schlittler's rise the past two years from unheralded prospect to Cy Young favorite has been phenomenal. He's putting together one of the best seasons ever for a Yankees starter -- no small achievement, given the franchise has had more than a little success in its history. He has given up one run or no runs in 20 of his 30 starts, already a franchise record, and has done so riding a heavy arsenal of upper 90s fastballs. He has thrown his four-seamer, cutter or sinker a combined 89.4% of his pitches -- and the league hasn't figured him out yet, as he has given up more than one run only once in his past nine starts. How he has changed the Yankees' fortunes: Aaron Judge ? Injured for much of the season. Max Fried ? Sat out nearly half the season. Carlos Rodon ? Sat out more than half the season. Gerrit Cole ? Didn't make his first start until May 22. With that group of stars missing a lot of time, Schlittler probably deserves MVP consideration aside from the Cy Young Award. He has been the dominant force all season in a rotation that leads the majors in ERA. As the offense struggled without Judge, Schlittler helped keep the Yankees within shouting distance of the Tampa Bay Rays in the American League East. Parker Messick , LHP, Cleveland Guardians Preseason: 7-8, 4.04 ERA, 129 IP, 118 SO, 1.4 WAR Season to date: 11-9, 2.53 ERA, 167 IP, 173 SO, 5.4 WAR Messick looked good in seven late-season starts in 2025, maintaining his rookie status for 2026, but with a fastball that had averaged 92.8 mph, he was viewed as more of a crafty lefty who might provide rotation depth rather than a potential frontline starter. Instead, he has been one of the league's top starters this season. And that fastball? He has pumped his four-seamer velocity up to 94.3 mph. Via Statcast pitch value metrics, it has been the most valuable pitch in baseball at plus-26 runs saved -- one run better even than Misiorowski's four-seam fastball. How he has changed the Guardians' fortunes : The rotation has kept the Guardians in the hunt for the AL Central title and a wild-card spot, ranking eighth in ERA and fourth in innings, as the offense and bullpen have had issues. Not only has Messick been excellent, he also has been durable, with the most innings by a rookie pitcher since 2019. As the Guardians have inched closer to the White Sox, Messick has been at his best, with a 2.05 ERA since the beginning of July. Miguel Vargas , 3B, Chicago White Sox Preseason: .238/.329/.406, 18 HR, 2.2 WAR 2026 to date: .248/.359/.477, 30 HR, 4.3 WAR MLB playoff tracker 2026 From current playoff matchups and clinching scenarios to league races and the postseason schedule, we've got it all. All things October &#187 Vargas was coming off a 1.9-WAR season with the White Sox in 2025, and the forecasts predicted more of the same. Vargas has instead powered his way to a 30-homer season thanks primarily to one simple change: He's swinging harder. His average bat speed has jumped from 70.6 mph to 74 mph, which has resulted in harder contact and more balls flying over the fence. The key is that he has maintained his reasonably low strikeout rate while also improving his walk rate. He also leads the AL in runs scored, which no White Sox player has done in a full season since Johnny Mostil in 1925 ( Tim Anderson tied for the lead in the 60-game season in 2020 and Frank Thomas led in the strike-shortened 1994 season). How he has changed the White Sox's fortunes: The White Sox ranked 23rd in the majors with 165 home runs in 2025 -- and 27th in runs scored. With Vargas, Colson Montgomery and Munetaka Murakami all having reached 30 home runs, the White Sox have hit 190 so far this season, which ranks sixth in the majors, and rank seventh in runs scored. The improved offense has ignited one of the most surprising seasons in White Sox history, with the club on the verge of making the playoffs only two years after a record-setting losing season in 2024. Jordan Walker , RF, St. Louis Cardinals Preseason: .239/.303/.387, 15 HR, 0.5 WAR 2026 to date: .282/.338/.490, 28 HR, 3.7 WAR Once a top-10 overall prospect in the game, Walker hit well as a 21-year-old rookie in 2023 but then struggled the next two seasons with a .211 average and 69 OPS+. Expectations weren't high for 2026 -- even though he just turned 24 in May -- but he finally translated his elite bat speed into some big numbers, including reaching 100 RBIs, pulling the ball in the air more often and making a big improvement against off-speed pitches and breaking balls. There is still room for improvement here as his chase rate (16th percentile) and whiff rate (12th percentile) lead to strikeouts and too many ground balls. His poor range in right field also drags down his overall WAR, although he does possess a powerful arm. If he can show PCA-like improvement in his swing decisions, Walker will do even more damage in the future. How he has changed the Cardinals' fortunes: The Cardinals have exceeded expectations and hung close all season in the wild-card race, although it will take a miracle run to finish the regular season to grab a spot. Still, with Walker, JJ Wetherholt and Alec Burleson , there is now a young offensive foundation -- and Wetherholt and Masyn Winn might both win Gold Gloves for their sterling up-the-middle defense. The Cardinals have been searching for a young power hitter to build around since Albert Pujols, and Walker looks as if he'll be that guy. Ty France , 1B, San Diego Padres Preseason: .251/.320/.380, 3 HR, 0.2 WAR 2026 to date: .290/.360/.507, 20 HR, 4.2 WAR Our first veteran on the list, France has had good seasons in the past, including a 4.2-WAR season with the Seattle Mariners in 2021, but he was worth just 0.4 WAR over the past two years as he played for four different teams. The Padres didn't even sign France until the middle of February -- and then only on a minor league contract. He made the roster after a strong spring training but started only one of the Padres' first 15 games before eventually becoming the starting first baseman. Ranking MLB playoff races Here's what you need to know about the battles to reach October as teams try to lock up a postseason spot. David Schoenfield &#187 What kind of season has he had? He's second to only Willson Contreras in WAR among all major league first basemen. The key: France has focused on hitting for more power, not only pulling the ball more often but hitting it harder when he does hit it in the air. He has done that while seeing his always-solid strikeout rate rise only five percentage points. How he has changed the Padres' fortunes: "I don't think anybody would have guessed that coming out of spring training," manager Craig Stammen said earlier this season about France's success. Indeed, he has been the Padres' best hitter -- and while the lineup has been excellent since the All-Star break, it flailed before that, so France especially helped keep the Padres afloat in the first half. They had ranked in the middle of the pack in offense at first base in 2025, but that was mostly Luis Arraez , who left as a free agent. France has filled what could have turned into a black hole, and without him, the Padres would be several wins behind the Diamondbacks in the wild-card race instead of neck-and-neck for that final spot. Eduardo Rodriguez , LHP, Arizona Diamondbacks Preseason: 8-8, 4.21 ERA, 133 IP, 119 SO, 1.3 WAR 2026 to date: 15-5, 2.55 ERA, 173 IP, 128 SO, 5.3 WAR Coming off their World Series appearance in 2023, the Diamondbacks signed the eight-year veteran Rodriguez to a four-year, $80 million contract. The first two years didn't go well, as he went a combined 12-13, making only 10 starts in 2024, and had an ERA over 5.00 in each. This season has probably been a little fluky as he has given up a .269 average on balls in play -- well below his career mark of .304 -- and posted a 2.55 ERA despite a low strikeout rate. But he has made some changes to his pitch usage, throwing his changeup and curveball more often while dropping his four-seamer and cutter usage. That seems to have helped the effectiveness of his four-seamer, as batters are hitting .200 against it after a .287 average in 2025. How he has changed the Diamondbacks' fortunes: They would be planning their offseason golf dates without him. The rest of the starting pitchers have combined for only 1.4 WAR and have gone 31-40. Lucky or not, Rodriguez's ERA is real -- and the Diamondbacks have gone 13-3 in his past 16 starts. Jake Bauers , 1B/OF, Milwaukee Brewers Preseason: .220/.322/.420, 12 HR, 0.7 WAR 2026 to date: .268/.395/.490, 24 HR, 3.0 WAR Bauers was an interesting prospect, reaching Triple-A at age 21 in the Rays' system, but he had never posted an above-average OPS+ in the majors until last season. Indeed, it's surprising the Brewers kept him around after he hit .199 in 2024. Now 30 years old, you can't really classify this as a breakout, but his Statcast page has red all over it: 96th percentile hard-hit rate, 94th percentile bat speed, 98th percentile walk rate, 96th percentile in expected wOBA. He leads the National League in OBP and ranks seventh in the majors in OPS. Maybe it's a career season, but there is nothing lucky about how he's putting up the numbers. How he has changed the Brewers' fortunes: The Brewers are still last in the majors in home runs, but Bauers leads the team while ranking second to Brice Turang in RBIs despite playing mostly against just right-handers. Like several of his teammates, he has performed exceptionally well with runners in scoring position, with a .989 OPS. He's also hitting .326 with a .991 OPS in high-leverage plate appearances, helping the Brewers to rank third in runs despite that lack of over-the-fence pop. Though he's not a good defensive player, Bauers has at least provided versatility, starting 75 games at first base and 39 in the outfield. He's not the team MVP with Misiorowski around, but Bauers has given the Brewers a legitimate middle-of-the-order hitter against right-handed pitching. Louis Varland , RHP, Toronto Blue Jays Preseason: 4-3, 2 saves, 3.51 ERA, 0.6 WAR 2026 to date: 5-5, 33 saves, 1.26 ERA, 3.4 WAR Postseason Baseball Challenge Fill out MLB postseason brackets for FREE! $10K in prizes. Make Your Picks Considering how the Blue Jays' 2025 season ended -- with Jeff Hoffman unable to close out the lead in Game 7 of the World Series -- the ninth inning was going to be a key issue for the Jays this year. Hoffman started the season in the closer role again, but after three blown saves by mid-April, Varland took over and has produced one of the best relief seasons in Blue Jays' history, pumping 99-mph fastballs, a knuckle-curveball and a near-unhittable changeup. That combo has induced a high rate of grounders -- 97th percentile -- that has kept the ball in the park (only two home runs given up), a nice change from Hoffman's home run issues last season. How he has changed the Blue Jays' fortunes : If Varland hadn't stepped up, who knows where the Jays would be. Yes, the mediocrity across the AL has kept them in the wild-card race, but considering the lineup has struggled all season and the rotation has battled injuries, the bullpen has been one area that manager John Schneider has been able to trust after those initial issues in April.
